objective: Find whether a simple, fixed KR stock-selection rule earns a higher risk-adjusted return net of costs than holding 069500.KS over 6-12 months, measured ONLY on signals recorded at the close they describe.
registrationStatement: Pre-registered before any signal of this study exists. Merging the change that adds this file is the authorization; the first eligible signal session is the first KR weekly decision session strictly after the KST date of that merge and not before firstEligibleSignalSessionFloor.
Every rule, horizon, cost, metric and decision threshold below is fixed here. A changed rule is a new study version with its own ledger; this one is never edited, rescored or restarted.
No result exists. Until the registered checks run, nothing may be described as predictive, and no book enters the official weekly decision, an order or a production weight.
historicalEvidenceStatement: The information is not new. Low downside volatility (registry F02/F01) and proximity to the 52-week high (registry A11) are families the closed KR historical programme (kr-alpha-atlas, Phase D: zero nominations) already measured with inconclusive readings; the KR lowvol sleeve was the one regional reading that cleared zero on its own (v2.21, secondary, not a finding).
The KR historical sample is spent and is NOT re-read by this study. What is new is the evidence: a prospective sample that did not exist when either hypothesis was formed.

The existing production ranking (longterm four-sleeve alpha) is the control, not a candidate: its KR ordering is not established (weekly-passive-first-v1 disclosure: rank-IC t 0.68) and the official KR decision is expected to hold 069500.KS.

hypotheses.CH_LOWVOL: Low-volatility anomaly: leverage-constrained investors overpay for volatile names, so the least downside-volatile large KR names earn more per unit of risk than the index.
hypotheses.CH_HIGH52: Anchoring to the 52-week high delays the reaction to good news, so large KR names trading closest to their 52-week high while above their 200-day average keep outperforming.

CH_LOWVOL.feature: risk.downsideVolPct of longTerm.regions.KR.validationCrossSection (252-session semi-deviation of negative daily returns, annualized, longterm.downside_vol_252)
CH_LOWVOL.requires: finite and positive, and the 252-return window proven on the exchange calendar: A fresh vendor download at record time (pipeline.datafeed.fetch_prices, auto_adjust, the production build's own call), aligned to the pinned KRX calendar by pipeline.kr_bar_integrity, must show every one of the window's sessions traded (253 closes for CH_LOWVOL, 252 for CH_HIGH52, the 200-day mean inside it) with no vendor row on a closed day inside it, AND must reproduce the artifact's own lastClose, feature and (CH_HIGH52) ma200 to the artifact's rounding. A missing, suspended or off-calendar session in the window is FEATURE_WINDOW_INCOMPLETE; a value the frame does not reproduce is FEATURE_VALUE_MISMATCH; both exclude the name from that book only. A name that needs this proof and has no vendor frame refuses the whole receipt (PRICE_FETCH_INCOMPLETE): a book is never formed on whichever names a partial download returned

CH_HIGH52.requires: finite in (0, 100.5]; details lastClose > details ma200 (a name whose 200-day average is undetermined is excluded, never assumed above); and the 252-session window proven on the exchange calendar (see CH_LOWVOL.requires)
CH_HIGH52.windowNote: features.price_52w_high and ma200 are rolling(252) / rolling(200) over vendor ROWS, so a history with a KRX session missing inside the last year carries a value spanning more than 252 sessions; the calendar proof above excludes it rather than adopting the production definition's row count

CTRL_MODEL5.feature: alpha of longTerm.regions.KR.validationCrossSection (production four-sleeve composite x evidence coverage)

universe.source: longTerm.regions.KR.validationCrossSection of the validated production artifact data/site-data.json built by .github/workflows/ledger.yml (production-eligible names: dataInsufficient excluded by longterm.build). The same rows feed every book.
rowRules: first occurrence of a ticker only
universe.missingRule: A missing, non-finite or out-of-range feature excludes the name from that book only and is counted by reason. Nothing is imputed, carried forward or replaced with 0.
universe.survivorship: The universe is the one the production build resolves at the signal date. Prospectively that is point-in-time by construction; a later delisting is graded through the outcome rules, never by dropping the name.

construction.thinCrossSection: fewer than minEligibleNames eligible names: the book holds no name and all five slots are 069500.KS (status THIN_CROSS_SECTION)

schedule.signalSessions: KR weekly decision sessions: a KR session whose next KR session falls in a later ISO week (prospective_receipt_core.is_weekly_decision_session)
schedule.artifactRule: the artifact's ^KS11 session equals the last KR session that was final (18:00 KST) at the artifact's generatedAt
schedule.receiptWindow: created by the writer's own clock after 18:00 KST of the signal session and before 09:00 KST of the next KR session (prospective_receipt_core.check_timing)
schedule.execution: close of the next KR session after the signal session (session 0)
schedule.runner: scripts/update_ledger.py (the paper-ledger step of .github/workflows/ledger.yml) calls scripts/record_kr_selection_challenger.run_all after its own work; any refusal is caught and never costs the paper ledger. No workflow file is changed (.github/workflows is tree-pinned by rp1-wp2-us-universe-v1).
schedule.expectedCadence: The 00:10 UTC cron starts about 04:30 UTC, inside the KRX session on weekdays, so weekday runs skip (ARTIFACT_NOT_BUILT_ON_A_FINAL_SESSION) and the Saturday run records Friday's session; Sunday's run is the backup inside the same window.

outcomeDefinition.priceBasis: vendor adjusted close (pipeline.datafeed.fetch_prices, auto_adjust) for every name and for 069500.KS, from one download at grading time, aligned to the pinned KRX calendar by pipeline.kr_bar_integrity
outcomeDefinition.nameReturn: close at the maturity session (horizon sessions after execution) / close at the execution session - 1
outcomeDefinition.notExecutable: a name SUSPENDED (zero volume) at the execution session cannot be bought; its slot is held in 069500.KS
outcomeDefinition.unresolved: a name with no vendor frame, no row or an invalid close at execution, or that did not trade on the maturity session itself, makes that book's cohort outcome None (NAME_OUTCOME_MISSING or TERMINAL_ECONOMICS_UNRESOLVED); it is never marked at an earlier close, dropped or renormalised
outcomeDefinition.netExcess: book return - 069500.KS return - stock legs (buy at execution, sell at maturity) - ETF legs of benchmark-held slots + the ETF control's own round trip
outcomeDefinition.costs: pipeline.weekly_decision.trade_cost_fraction('KR', date, ...): commission + half spread per leg, dated statutory sell tax on stock sells, no tax on ETF sells (benchmark_alpha.REALISTIC_COSTS)
outcomeDefinition.retry: Two classes. PROVIDER_DATA_UNAVAILABLE (the benchmark or a held name has no vendor frame, a session with no row, or an invalid close: an empty or partial download) is DEFERRED at any date: nothing is written, every later run regrades it from a fresh download, and its retryable state is kept in outcome-pending.json, outside the append-only ledgers and never evidence. An empty or partial vendor answer is never read as a delisting or a terminal event. ECONOMIC_UNRESOLVED (the vendor served the maturity session and it shows zero volume) is DEFERRED until the (horizon + 5)-th KR session after execution is final and then written (FINAL_UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RETRY, with the reasons) and counted as None. A cohort containing a receipt the provider never serves stays ungraded; closing it needs an independent source for the terminal event, which is an owner decision and not a recorder default

assessment.interim: No outcome statistic is published before a registered check. Turnover (a signal-time fact) is reported at any time.

harmCheck.rule: on the first 52 receipts, once all are graded at H126: STOPPED_HARM if the Newey-West 95% upper bound of mean net excess vs 069500.KS is below 0; INCONCLUSIVE_DATA if more than 5 outcomes are None

riskPath.notExecutable: a newly chosen name SUSPENDED (served row, zero volume) on a rebalance session is held as 069500.KS for that period, the same rule as outcomeDefinition.notExecutable, with the same legs charged; a missing row or invalid close on a rebalance session, or a held name without a traded close on any marking day, makes the path INCOMPLETE

primary.rule: on the first 104 receipts, once all are graded at H252 and H126: SUPPORTED only if (1) the one-sided 98.75% (Bonferroni over two challengers) Newey-West lower bound of mean H252 net excess vs 069500.KS is above 0, (2) the mean H126 net excess is above 0, (3) the mean H252 net excess vs CTRL_MODEL5 is above 0, and (4) the 4-weekly rebalanced daily paper path has Sharpe >= 069500.KS and |max drawdown| <= 1.25 x 069500.KS over the same sessions; NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise; INCONCLUSIVE_DATA if more than 10 outcomes are None in ANY series a check reads (the H252 series, the H126 series, or the paired H252 comparison with CTRL_MODEL5, each counted on its own valid pairs) or the risk path is incomplete or its Sharpe or drawdown is undefined

assessment.inference: kelly_portfolio._newey_west_stats on the receipt-dated series (Bartlett HAC, lag from the horizon in observations of this series); overlapping weekly cohorts are never counted as independent
assessment.afterVerdict: A SUPPORTED verdict is development evidence for one owner decision, never an automatic promotion. STOPPED_HARM or NOT_SUPPORTED closes this version; recording may continue for the record but no rule is changed to rescue it.

turnover: names replaced per weekly receipt and per path rebalance, as a share of five slots (weights retargeted are not turnover here)
